newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CEPA says Southern deal delayed.
newsitem.headline: CEPA says Southern deal delayed.

text.p: Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd said on Tuesday it has extended the closing date for the acquisition by Southern Electric International of a major stake in the Hong Kong-based company because of paperwork delays.

"Although considerable progress has been made in obtaining a significant number of such consents in principle and no negative responses have been received to date... largely as a result of the logistics of obtaining formally documented Consents, the original expected timetable requires extension," CEPA said.
The last day for trading in CEPA shares has been revised to January 10, from the original December 11, it said in a statement said on Tuesday.
The scheme effective date has been extended to January 29 from December 28, and the withdrawal of CEPA's Hong Kong listing will be effective January 30, delayed from December 30, it said.
CEPA said "credit agreements relating to CEPA's power project at Sual, the Philippines, shall have been satisfied, waived or modified in a manner satisfactory to the lenders."
CEPA said "discussions with the lenders are progressing satisfactorily with no adverse responses received to date."

Based on the revised expected timetable and following the delisting, the cash entitlements under the first option and the cash and other entitlements under the second option, are expected to be posted on or before January 31, extending from December 31, it added.
